title: They increase peace (Berakhot 64a)
hookLine: the tractate ends: the wise increase peace in the world
tomorrow: you finished a whole book. how do you say goodbye to it?

lines: THE LAST MESSAGE SAYS A LOT.
cards: The last message in a group chat after a fight says a lot. A thumbs-up. A long paragraph.
Silence. Endings tell you what something was for. Berakhot, the whole tractate of blessings, has to end somewhere.
It started at night, with the Shema. It could have ended on a law or a warning. Instead its last lines are about people who learn, and its very last word is peace.

teach.b: Here's the ending, in plain words. Rabbi Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Hanina: those who learn Torah increase peace in the world.

His proof is Isaiah: "And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children." Then a small, playful move. Don't read banayikh, your children, read bonayikh, your builders.
Same Hebrew letters, a different word. The ones who learn are builders, and what they build is peace. Then the page strings psalms together, one after another.
"Great peace have they that love Thy law; and there is no stumbling for them." Peace within your walls, for the sake of my brothers and friends.
And the last one is from Psalm 29: "The LORD will give strength unto His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace."
Look at that: strength, yesterday's word, then peace. Strength isn't the goal.
It's what peace is built with. Something to tell a friend tonight: in Hebrew that final word, bashalom, with peace, closes the whole tractate of blessings.

how: The passage 'those who learn Torah increase peace in the world' (from the end of Berakhot) appears in the siddur and is said in some communities near the end of the Shabbat morning service.

o: a blessing said when a war or fight is over
a rule that scholars must never argue with anyone
the last teaching of Berakhot: learners build peace

games.q: how Berakhot ends — tap the pairs.

s: Berakhot ends with a law about blessings
it ends with people who learn, and its last word is peace.
the sages reread 'your children' as 'your builders'
banayikh to bonayikh: same Hebrew letters, a different word.
in the last verse, strength and peace are opposites
God gives strength, then blesses with peace: strength is what peace is built with.

games.q: two friends are fighting and both want you on their side. what would the end of Berakhot call you to be?
o: a builder: talk to each, find what they still share.
a judge: hear both, then say who was right.
a bystander: stay quiet until it blows over.
games.why: those who learn increase peace, and the sages call them builders. peace here is made, not waited for or won.

practice: Think of someone you've bumped against lately, or drifted from. Write them one short text that builds instead of wins: a thank you, an I'm sorry, a how are you. Read it once slowly, and send it only if it feels right.

wordCard.voice: They increase peace. The last teaching in Berakhot: those who learn are builders, and they build peace.

orig.note: Hebrew: your builders. the sages' rereading of banayikh, your children, in Isaiah 54:13.

carryVoice: Keep this one: they increase peace, builders, not winners. Forty-six of fifty, and a good week.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 64a (Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Hanina: Torah scholars increase peace in the world; do not read banayikh but bonayikh; the closing verses)
